question: The set of \(x\)-values satisfying the inequality \(2\le|x-1|\le5\) is:
solution:
The quantity \(|x-1|\) is the distance from \(x\) to \(1\) on the number line. The inequality requires that distance to be between \(2\) and \(5\), including both bounds.

To the left of \(1\), the permitted points run from \(1-5=-4\) to \(1-2=-1\). To the right, they run from \(1+2=3\) to \(1+5=6\).

Every permitted point lies on one of these two sides, and every point in these intervals has the required distance. Hence the complete solution is
\[
\boxed{-4\le x\le-1\quad\text{or}\quad3\le x\le6},
\]
choice \(\boxed{\text{A}}\).

edges.reason: The actual number-line criterion checks an origin, a designated direction and a unit. A designated positive direction is an orientation convention; it does not require the full signed-number classification or negative contexts asserted by Gemini.
edges.scope: Origin, designated orientation and unit as the three structural elements of a number line

edges.reason: Absolute value is defined as the distance from a point to the origin. That definition presupposes a number line with an origin and a unit length, which give distance its meaning.
edges.scope: geometric meaning of absolute value as distance to origin

edges.reason: The actual computational rule can be stated piecewise and gives both solutions of |x|=a for a positive a. Gemini treats the geometry/definition node as unavoidable, but this geometry-specific endpoint is not needed to apply that supplied rule.
edges.scope: Geometric distance interpretation as preparation for the piecewise absolute-value computation rule

edges.reason: The plotted object is the set of all values making an inequality true; solution and solution-set meanings are required.

The piecewise algebra route uses the sign-based formula; a distance route can avoid that decomposition. Absolute magnitude is shared meaning. Sign rewriting and affine inequality solving belong only to the sign-interval route; a single-distance bound can instead be read directly on the number line.
edges.scope: replace each absolute value on complete sign intervals

edges.reason: Both sign-interval and geometric routes use the absolute-value quantity, distinct from an unsigned affine expression. Absolute magnitude is shared meaning. Sign rewriting and affine inequality solving belong only to the sign-interval route; a single-distance bound can instead be read directly on the number line.
edges.scope: absolute value as a nonnegative distance
